direct_plugin_workload.origin: Standalone Python sqlite3 connection loads the sqlite_ivm dylib directly; SQL is handwritten parity recursion, with no Sprefa process or generated SQL.
direct_plugin_workload.sql: WITH RECURSIVE parity(side,n) AS (SELECT 0,n FROM starts UNION SELECT 0,e.b FROM parity p JOIN edges e ON p.n=e.a WHERE p.side=1 UNION SELECT 1,e.b FROM parity p JOIN edges e ON p.n=e.a WHERE p.side=0), even(n) AS (SELECT n FROM parity WHERE side=0), odd(n) AS (SELECT n FROM parity WHERE side=1) SELECT n FROM odd
direct_plugin_workload.attribution: prepare_start/end spans originate in sqlite_ivm src/0g_statements.rs around rusqlite db.prepare or db.prepare_cached. SQLite reprepare is SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_REPREPARE from hafley-observe PROFILE; the direct case includes schema creation and temp scratch-table changes.

compiler_shaped_plugin_workload.origin: Sprefa c2 fixture emitted SQL, then sqlite_ivm compiled and executed its maintenance statements.

interpretation: The large first-versus-second difference at the same sqlite_ivm call site and identical SQL supports SQLite compilation cost on the first cached prepare. Every prepare_cached API call emits a prepare span, including cache hits; 18,813 is not a count of SQLite compilations. The standalone plugin case proves instrumentation and prepare/reprepare behavior without Sprefa, but its 4.3 KB maximum SQL does not reproduce the compiler-shaped 130+ KB cost.
measurement_scope: Span times contain JSON tracing overhead and are single-run diagnostic measurements. Raw traces are local /private/tmp artifacts, not committed.
